verdict: The copy is best-in-class: every heading is a two-beat line that lands at 1440 and 390, the voice is plain and X-native (lowercase, $BTC, ngl, 'bits of fluff'), claims are honest, pricing is exact, and all 10 of my own lines produced true, well-explained results in the Try box and final input. What is left is small P2 phrasing polish below the first read of any section; no P0 or P1.

issues.where: Studio card, first bullet: 'Up to 8 client voices. Yours is included.'
issues.problem: Ambiguous on two counts: is your own voice one of the 8, and is it billed at $18 like a client? A ghostwriter doing the maths has to guess.
issues.fix: Say it outright, e.g. 'Up to 8 client voices. Your own voice is free on top.' (or whichever is true: 'Your own counts as one.').

issues.where: Voice card under 'ngl eth looks strong here.': 'Put back once already. Once more and it stays.'
issues.problem: Subject-less and clipped; a first-time visitor has to work out who put what back before the 'it learns' idea lands.
issues.fix: Name the word and the actor: 'You put “ngl” back once. Once more and it stays for good.'

issues.where: 'Is it just AI writing, like ChatGPT?' answer
issues.problem: At roughly 85 words in two paragraphs it is the one answer that breaks the page's short-answer promise ('Short answers to what people ask first'), and the opening 'It's AI that edits your line, and drafts rewrites and replies' reads as a list before the point.
issues.fix: Cut to about 45 words: 'It edits your line; it doesn't write for you. Sharpen cuts fluff and puts the point first. Rewrites build three takes from your own words, and a check rejects any that change your facts. The demo here runs on your device; in the app, Claude makes the edit. Nothing goes out until you send it.'

issues.where: Sheet, after entering an email: 'Open the working app on claude.ai (demo data)'
issues.problem: Naming claude.ai as the host exposes the build tooling in the one place a visitor has just shown intent; it reads as internal, not as product voice.
issues.fix: Change the label to 'Open the working demo (sample data)' and keep the destination as is.

issues.where: Try box, pasting a pure announcement such as 'We're thrilled to share some huge news with you all today'
issues.problem: The headline state reads 'Kept as written' for the most recognisable fluff line there is; the explanation underneath is honest and good, but the label undersells that fluff was found.
issues.fix: Change the state label for the marked-not-cut case to 'Marked 1 bit of fluff · Your call' so the visitor sees it was caught before reading why it was not removed.
